overall: The AG found the Arlington Tree Committee did not violate the Open Meeting Law. October 8 allegations were untimely, and the remaining c.87, notice, and remarks claims fell outside the OML, with no serial deliberation found.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Committee gave insufficient notice of its October 8, 2025 meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Because the complaint was filed with the Committee on December 18, 2025, more than 30 days after the date of the alleged violations, we find that these allegations are untimely and we decline to review them.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Committee let individuals make defaming and disparaging remarks about the complainant at the October 8, 2025 meeting.
allegations.key_passage: When an alleged violation occurs during an open session, the alleged violation is reasonably discoverable at the time it occurs.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged defaming and disparaging remarks against the complainant were allowed at the November 19, 2025 meeting.
allegations.key_passage: We have previously declined to review complaints alleging that a public body has violated c. 87, or that a public body subjected a complainant to hostile treatment.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged insufficient notice to the complainant of the November 19, 2025 meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, even if true, an allegation that the Committee did not provide sufficient notice to the complainant would not constitute a violation of the Open Meeting Law and we decline to review it.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the conduct of the meetings violated G.L. c. 87, the shade tree statute.
allegations.key_passage: Even if true, these allegations would not constitute a violation of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged Committee members deliberated outside a meeting, citing discussion of a letter from the Tree Warden around the November 19 meeting.
allegations.key_passage: To the extent the complaint alleges that the Committee deliberated outside of a properly noticed meeting via serial communication facilitated by the Tree Warden, we find no evidence of such serial deliberation.

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
